column4: Cagayan Bridge Projects for Economic Development
column6: Network Development Program -  Construction of By-pass and Diversion Roads
column7: Department of Public Works and Highways
column8:
Turkey/Design & Build Construction of 3 bridges and approaches in the Province of Cagayan, namely: 

A. Solana-Bagay Bridge, Solana, Cagayan - The bridge serves as an alternate bridge to the 45-year-old Buntun Bridge. Currently, there are only two bridges traversing the Cagayan River in the province of Cagayan, the Buntun Bridge in the south and the Magapit Bridge in the mid-section of the province. The Solana-Bagay Bridge also serves as a major bridge connecting the eastern to the western part of the province of Cagayan in addition to its role of easing traffic congestion in Tuguegarao City being connected to the ongoing by-pass road to the west of the City.  It is a construction of 2,554 linear meter 2-lane bridge composed of conventional span and arch span.

B. Alcala Bridge, Tupang, Alcala, in Cagayan - The bridge connects the first district to the 2nd district of the province. It will complement the ongoing effort to establish the road network for Alcala, Piat, Tuao, Sto. Nino, Lasam, and Allacapan in the west of the province and will strengthen its linkage to the provinces of Kalinga and Apayao. It also serves as a major bridge in case of massive flooding occurrence in the province. It is a construction of a 2-lane, 450 linear meter, 2 Bridge Type - Double Truss Arch and a Truss Girder.

C. Pinacanauan Bridge, Tuguegarao, Cagayan - The bridge will serve as a bypass bridge that will connect directly to the Maharlika highway in Capatan, Tuguegarao City. The bridge component includes a dike road which also serves as a flood mitigation structure that will connect the city's main CBD to the eastern barangays which are isolated during flooding occurrence. It is a construction of a 4-lane, 450 linear meter, 3 Bridge Type - Double Truss Arch and a Truss Girder.

column4: Strengthening Palawan Landscape Governance Program for Recovery, Resiliency, and Self-Sufficiency in the Age of Pandemics and Rapidly Changing Climate
column6: Palawan Environmentally Critical Areas Network (ECAN) Management Program
column7: Palawan Council for Sustainable Development Staff
column8:
This proposal shall bring to the existing programs/projects/activities of the PCSD the technologies and innovations from best practices on environment and natural resources management for a healthy and fully functioning environment. These include innovations in decision support tools generated from past projects such as the Capturing Coral Reef and Related Ecosystem Services (CCRES, World Bank) and the Wealth Accounting and Valuation of Ecosystem Services (WAVES, World Bank); innovative management from the Strengthening the Marine Protected Areas to Conserve Marine Key Biodiversity Areas in the Philippines (SMARTSEAS Project, USAID), Fish Right Program (USAID), Protect Wildlife Project (USAID), Forest Foundation Philippines (FPE), among others. Furthermore, the proposed expansion will include new researches on wildlife for management and policy, and innovative education strategies. The project also includes improvement of structures and facilities of the agency in the main office and its district offices, in order to cater to the growing demand of Palawan's constituents for government services. 

This project is composed of three components: 
1.	Construction and Improvement of PCSDS Buildings 
2.	Research
3.	Support to Operations

column8: The Western Visayas Medical Center (WVMC) proposal for the Heart and Lung Center is a significant infrastructure project tailored to meet the healthcare needs of the Western Visayas region in the Philippines. column4: Learning Resource Centers for Inclusive Education (LRC-IE)
column6: Basic Education Facilities
column7: Department of Education
column8:
One of the significant challenges identified in the Regional Education Development Plan (REDP) of DepEd Region IX is the severe shortage of centers and other facilities under the Inclusive Education Program. This program encompasses learners from the Special Needs Education (SNED), Arabic Language and Islamic Values Education (ALIVE), Indigenous Peoples Education (IPED), and Alternative Learning System (ALS). Schools are struggling to accommodate these learners due to the lack of necessary facilities. During the 2022-2023 school year, the DepEd Central Office set a target of 119,833 learners for the Inclusive Education Program in Region IX. However, the actual number of enrolled learners reached
200,261, representing 167% of the target. Consequently, many learners were integrated into regular classes due to the shortage of specialized teachers, centers, and materials essential for inclusive education.

This project aims to establish specialized centers equipped with the resources and technologies required to support inclusive education. These centers provide tailored educational materials and assistive technologies to ensure that all students, including those with disabilities, have access to quality education.
